title: One Render, Four Platforms: Automated Video Distribution | vitalii.no
description:
How a single video reaches YouTube, LinkedIn, Instagram Reels and Facebook from one trigger, in two minutes instead of forty-five.

Manually adapting one video for four platforms was a genuine time sink. YouTube wants 16:9, Instagram Reels wants 9:16, LinkedIn caps MP4 uploads under 200MB, and every platform speaks its own API. Re-encoding, resizing and clicking through four separate upload flows ate 30 to 45 minutes per video.

The pipeline uses Remotion to render two distinct NewsVideo versions: 1080x1920 vertical for Reels and 1920x1080 horizontal for YouTube, LinkedIn and Facebook. GitHub Actions then orchestrates distribution through dedicated workflows: process-video.yml drives the YouTube Data API v3, with linkedin-video.yml, instagram-video.yml and facebook-video.yml handling the rest through the Graph API. MTKruto pulls large source videos straight from Telegram, up to 2GB, bypassing the Bot API's 20MB ceiling. If any platform upload fails, a fallback posts a Telegram embed instead of dropping the content.

Distribution time fell from 30-45 minutes to 2-3 minutes of monitoring, and one trigger now reaches four audiences. Running the heavy work in GitHub Actions also sidesteps the 256MB /tmp limit on Supabase Edge Functions, so 2GB files are no longer an infrastructure problem.
